Anytype has tables now, simple, no formulas yet. Plan to add formulas to databases - it's one of the top requested features on our forum (co-founder anytype).

(Notion employee) The Anytype model is really cool - they've rebuilt Lotus Notes with 21st century E2E encrypted protocols... However they also demonstrate the complexity and tradeoffs of the E2E approach. Anytype has been a work-in-progress since at least 2019, still lacking collaboration and browser version.

As a teacher I just can't use Notion or any other US-service due to GDPR concerns. I hope AnyType copies as many good Notion features so I can leave Notion and its abysmal performance and lack of offline mode.

We don't offer a browser version. Instead, we have an Electron-based cross-platform app for Windows, Linux, macOS, plus native iOS and Android apps. Creating a browser version is challenging because our business logic relies on a Go middleware library.

I found Anytype a few months ago and thought 'wow maybe I can ditch Turtl and just use this.' A few things bugged me: it's source-available license, you can't share with others yet, and they call it e2e encrypted but data lives unencrypted on-disk. That said, the interface and utility are amazing, kind of like Notion mixed with a personal database, and sync between devices worked great.

(Anytype team) All your data in Anytype is encrypted at rest; only the indexes are not encrypted currently. We have plans to also encrypt the indexes. Our protocol is p2p and works well in local networks - install on desktop and mobile with the same phrase and data syncs without a central server.
I consistently find myself in need of a 'merge feature' when re-importing cleaned CSV data into Anytype database objects - the larger the database becomes, the more crucial this feature is.
I signed up for early access but I'm not too hopeful. There's some blockchain-esque use of words... it's impossible to get any clue of how it works without signing up.
Anytype works on a peer-to-peer stack (as torrents), so there is no blockchain needed at this stage (Anytype team response to DAO/blockchain questions).
